sonnet.problem: The story card says the LORD has "one last word," but the text never says this is His last word. The speech in 5:9-10 is just one more statement, and the passage doesn't mark it as the final one.
sonnet.rule: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

sonnet.problem: Card 14's question already states that the restitution "goes to the priest." That gives away the answer to card 16 ("the priest"). The question also rewords the verse's "bring to the priest" as "bring in" to hide the answer, so the priest is the only believable pick next to "elders" and "judges."
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The True statement mostly restates card 10, which already established "full restitution" plus "a fifth." The only new part, that it goes to the person he wronged, is easy to infer from the setup. It makes the same point as card 10.
sonnet.rule: A True statement never just repeats the card before it. ... Two lines that make the same point get one question.
